laplacian.title: Variance of Laplacian (Default / Fast)
laplacian.how_it_works: 🔬 How It Works: Applies a 2D Laplacian operator (∇²I) over the grayscale luminance channel to measure edge second-derivatives. Sharp images contain steep intensity transitions (high variance), while blurry images produce smooth gradients (low variance).
laplacian.detects: 🎯 Detects: General defocus blur & soft edge variance across the whole photo.
laplacian.pros: ✅ Pros: Ultra-fast execution, extremely low CPU memory footprint, ideal for rapid first-pass culling across thousands of photos.
laplacian.cons: ⚠️ Cons: Can mistake flat low-texture scenes (flat sky, plain walls) or intentional background bokeh for blur.
laplacian.best_for: 💡 Best For: General photography, landscape, studio, and rapid batch filtering.

ai_subject.title: AI Subject Focus (YOLO + ROI + Patch Grid)
ai_subject.how_it_works: 🔬 How It Works: Runs YOLOv8 AI object detection to locate the main subject bounding box, then evaluates 3 crop layers (Full Subject, Head & Eye Zone, Subject Core) using 95th percentile Laplacian + Sobel gradient energy. Includes an 8x8 patch grid bokeh protection engine. Falls back to center-60% ROI crop when no AI detection is available.
ai_subject.detects: 🎯 Detects: Subject-aware focus sharpness — eyes, head, beak, and facial details within AI-detected bounding boxes.
ai_subject.pros: ✅ Pros: 100% automated AI subject localization with bokeh immunity. Completely ignores smooth background blur; rewards pin-sharp bird & wildlife eyes/head/beak details. Absorbs center-ROI and patch variance methods as internal fallback layers.
ai_subject.cons: ⚠️ Cons: Slightly higher per-photo inference time (~25ms). Requires YOLO model download on first use.
ai_subject.best_for: 💡 Best For: Birding, wildlife, shallow depth-of-field portraits, off-center subjects, macro, and heavy background bokeh.

fft.title: FFT Frequency Analysis (Motion Blur)
fft.how_it_works: 🔬 How It Works: Transforms image into 2D frequency domain using Fast Fourier Transform. Masks out central low frequencies and calculates the ratio of high-frequency magnitude spectrum energy.
fft.detects: 🎯 Detects: High-frequency spectrum energy ratio (distinguishes motion blur/camera shake from soft focus).
fft.pros: ✅ Pros: Excellent at detecting directional motion blur, hand-shake, and subject movement that edge operators miss.
fft.cons: ⚠️ Cons: Higher computational cost due to 2D Fast Fourier Transforms.
fft.best_for: 💡 Best For: Action shots, handheld low-light photos, and camera shake detection.

dhash.title: Perceptual Hash (dHash)
dhash.how_it_works: 🔬 How It Works: Downsamples image to 9x8 grayscale, compares adjacent column luminance values to generate a 64-bit binary perceptual hash bit vector, and calculates bitwise XOR Hamming distance between images.
dhash.detects: 🎯 Detects: Near-identical photos, crops, exposure tweaks & burst shots.
dhash.pros: ✅ Pros: Ultra-fast, highly accurate visual similarity comparison across different image formats and exposure tweaks.
dhash.cons: ⚠️ Cons: Might miss extreme subject pose variations in high-speed burst shots.
dhash.thresh_guide: 📊 Threshold Guide: 1-4 bits = Nearly identical. 6-8 bits = Same image with minor edits / wildlife bursts. >12 bits = Different images.
dhash.best_for: 💡 Best For: General duplicate removal, wildlife burst shots, and near-identical photo culling.

md5.title: Exact File Hash (MD5)
md5.how_it_works: 🔬 How It Works: Computes MD5 checksum on the initial file bytes combined with file byte size. Identifies byte-for-byte exact file duplicates.
md5.pros: ✅ Pros: Zero false positives. Instantly finds byte-level copies ('Copy of...', identical exports).
md5.cons: ⚠️ Cons: Misses edited, re-saved, or re-compressed JPEG variations.
md5.thresh_guide: 📊 Threshold Guide: Fixed exact byte match. No slider threshold needed.
md5.best_for: 💡 Best For: Cleaning duplicate file exports and exact backup copies.

burst_time.title: Burst Time Window
burst_time.how_it_works: 🔬 How It Works: Reads EXIF 'date_taken' timestamps (or file creation times) and groups consecutive photos captured within a configurable delta time window T.
burst_time.detects: 🎯 Detects: Rapid-fire camera burst sequences based on EXIF capture timestamp.
burst_time.pros: ✅ Pros: Groups high-speed burst shots regardless of visual pose changes or subject movement.
burst_time.cons: ⚠️ Cons: Requires valid EXIF date/time metadata in image files.
burst_time.thresh_guide: 📊 Threshold Guide: 0.5s - 1.0s = High-speed sports/birds. 2.0s - 3.0s = General burst sequences.
burst_time.best_for: 💡 Best For: Sports, action, and bird flight burst sequences.
